text: When Michael was six. <break time="0.8s" /> He asked why he could not call Helen Mummy. <break time="0.8s" /> As other boys called their mothers. <break time="0.8s" /> And she gently explained. <break time="0.8s" /> That she was only his auntie. <break time="0.8s" /> Since he was so eager, however. <break time="0.8s" /> She allowed him to use the word. <break time="0.8s" /> At bedtime. <break time="0.8s" /> As a private pet name. <break time="0.8s" /> A secret to be shared. <break time="0.8s" /> Only between the two of them. <break time="0.8s" /> Michael kept the secret faithfully. <break time="0.8s" /> But when he discovered. <break time="0.8s" /> That Helen had told her friends about it. <break time="0.8s" /> He flew into a furious rage. <break time="0.8s" /> That astonished her. <break time="0.8s" /> Why did you tell. <break time="0.8s" /> He cried at the end of the storm. <break time="0.8s" /> And he declared. <break time="0.8s" /> That he would never call her Mummy again. <break time="0.8s" /> Not even at bedtime. <break time="0.8s" /> At ten. <break time="0.8s" /> After two terms at a preparatory school. <break time="0.8s" /> Michael came to understand. <break time="0.8s" /> The truth about his birth. <break time="0.8s" /> And he wondered anxiously. <break time="0.8s" /> Whether Helen would think less of him. <break time="0.8s" /> Far from pushing him away. <break time="0.8s" /> Helen reassured him so tenderly. <break time="0.8s" /> That the two of them grew closer than ever. <break time="0.8s" /> And the subject was not raised again. <break time="0.8s" /> For years. <break time="0.8s" /> Later when he lay delirious with measles. <break time="0.8s" /> At his public school. <break time="0.8s" /> The old question returned. <break time="0.8s" /> In his fever. <break time="0.8s" /> And once more Helen calmed and comforted him. <break time="0.8s" /> Michael grew into a clever young man. <break time="0.8s" /> And in the summer of 1914. <break time="0.8s" /> He was looking forward. <break time="0.8s" /> To going up to Oxford. <break time="0.8s" /> With a scholarship in October.
